pages.text: "Grandma, there are so many people!" Mei the timid baby goat held Grandma's hand tight. The square was full for the autumn market. A tall bell tower stood in the center.
A delicious smell drifted from somewhere. "I want roasted chestnuts! Just one bag!" Grandma led the way. "All right. Let's buy some over there."
Mei's feet followed the smell first, slipping between people's legs. Grandma's hand slipped out of Mei's.
By the chestnut cart, Mei looked back. No Grandma. Only unfamiliar grown-ups' backs and bundles. Mei's heart thumped.
Mei ran between the people for a long time, but saw no familiar face. "Grandma!" Mei stopped still, holding both scarf ends tightly.
Then, overhead, the bell rang. Dong! Mei looked up quickly. Above everyone's heads was the top of the bell tower.
Mei walked to the tower. Grandma Bear was already there. Twice as tall as Mei, she could be seen over the crowd. "Mei! At the bell tower, wait!" Grandma hugged Mei warmly.
"You can see the tower from anywhere in the square," Grandma said, pointing up. "Running takes you farther away. Stand here, and I'll come find you." Mei nodded.
Market day came again. As soon as Mei entered the square, they looked for the bell tower. "One, stop! Two, find the tower! Three, wait below it!" Grandma's hand stayed firmly in Mei's.

Grandma lifted Mei into her arms and gave them a bag of roasted chestnuts. Even if you get lost, wait at the bell tower and you can meet again. "At the bell tower, wait!" Mei blew gently on the hot chestnuts.
